name: Victor Olsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for a side. This is confidential. Walk me through a normal day at Foxbridge.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The kettle goes on before the first client file. I'm Victor Olsen, forty-three, and I handle small-trader accounts and tax returns, mostly receipts that arrive in carrier bags. I finished a bachelor's in accounting as an adult after years in a print shop, so I'm still a junior and need my supervisor on tricky tax codes. I use the firm's AI letter checker every day because it saves me from typing the same explanation again.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What feels good about the work, and what drains you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I like turning a bag of scraps into a set of numbers a trader understands. I don't like making the supervisor correct me twice. Mireya works at the postal depot; our two schoolchildren are seven and fourteen, and the mortgage takes most of our combined pay. I earn near the bottom for this job, we have less than a month saved, and there are few similar firms near home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could believe this, though the tool at my desk feels more useful than hype. It catches missing dates in client letters, and I use it every day, but it still guesses wrong about odd expenses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the other juniors to use the time saved to check the source record. I'd tell the partners that faster letters ought to mean paid practice on the hard returns, not another target raised on the noticeboard.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The job might survive, but our house runs close to empty. I'm forty-three and still junior at Foxbridge Accounts after finishing an accounting bachelor's as an adult. Mireya's postal wage and my low pay cover the mortgage and two schoolchildren, with less than a month saved and few nearby firms to try.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep using the letter checker and have my supervisor sign off on the returns I find tricky. I'd move the grocery order to the discount shop and hold forty a month in cash if prices stay near this level. In the first year of a plateau, I'd ask for one paid hour each week to go over my tax-code mistakes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the bills, even though I enjoy the tool. My son needs new glasses, and the eye appointment is already on the calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill is pressing right now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The glasses quote is a hundred and twenty, which is almost the spare cash we have this month. I'd buy them before putting forty in the tin. A little faster typing doesn't pay the optician.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you ask for learning time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd bring my correction list to my supervisor rather than pretend the checker has made me an expert. Some tax codes still trip me up. If I get the paid hour, I can work through those while the client queue stays covered.

say: I would use **saved minutes** for source checks.
I would ask for **paid practice** on difficult tax returns.
think: Our **mortgage and glasses bill** strain the month.
Few **nearby firms** make my junior pay hard to challenge.
do: Keep **daily letter checks** and supervisor sign-off.
Buy my son’s **glasses** before setting aside forty.
Ask for **one paid hour** weekly on tax-code corrections.
feel: I feel **anxious** about bills despite steady work.
S0.quote: A little faster typing doesn't pay the optician.
fieldNote: The **glasses bill** outranks a proposed cash transfer in an already thin household budget.
His **daily AI use** helps with letters, but he still relies on a supervisor for tax codes.

steps.text: Keep daily AI letter checks and supervisor sign-off on returns
Save forty monthly after glasses if discount groceries leave cash
Study tax-code corrections with supervisor if paid hour approved

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This is the part of my day that has a name on it: checking, writing and answering clients. The tool could take those before I have got good at the exceptions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At work I'd ask the staff association to see the new targets before anyone loses hours. I'd tell friends that a good firm should pay for people to learn the tool it wants them to use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might be the junior who stays because I already use AI daily, but the partner could keep the faster colleague instead. My own hours could still fall, and we cannot carry the mortgage on Mireya's postal wage alone. There are too few local accounting desks to treat that lightly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd offer to test the new checking system on fifteen tax returns and keep a list of wrong flags. I'd ask for paid time to learn the review screen, then show the results to the staff association. If the partners still cut my hours, I'd apply for the funded hospital billing vacancy only if its wage covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, even while I want to try the system. Being first to click a button is not the same as being last to lose a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your daughter?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My daughter has started asking whether we can pay for her school camp. I would tell her we need the bill in writing before saying yes. I cannot promise a camp fee while my hours are being discussed behind a closed door.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What evidence would you show the partners?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A wrong flag on a tax return can send a client a frightening letter. I'd save the examples with the original invoices so anyone can check them. The partners should see errors and wage effects in the same meeting.

say: I would seek **open targets** before the partners cut junior hours or raise the client queue.
I would demand **paid tool learning** for affected staff.
think: My **hours** may shrink despite using AI daily on letters and client files.
Mireya’s **postal wage** cannot cover the mortgage alone.
do: Test **fifteen returns** and log wrong AI flags.
Ask for **paid review training** and share results with staff.
Apply for **funded hospital billing** if hours fall and pay covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost hours and school costs.
S1.quote: Being first to click a button is not the same as being last to lose a wage.
fieldNote: His **early tool use** does not eliminate risk to junior hours or household income.
The **fifteen-return test** creates specific evidence for a staff meeting on errors and targets.

steps.text: Learn new review system using fifteen returns with paid training
Bring error and staffing evidence to staff association
Apply for funded hospital billing vacancy if hours fall and pay covers mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 is a short runway for someone who only recently got an accounting desk. If full AGI can do nearly all the thinking cheaper, I doubt my junior post survives one more filing season.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the government owes workers a wage bridge when a whole job type goes. I'd ask our staff association to demand dates, notice and a share of the gains before the partners cut us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect to lose my accounting job in the first year after 2028. My day is spent at a screen, so robots arriving around 2031 do not give me extra time. Mireya's postal wage cannot carry the mortgage, and our savings would not last a month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd cancel the weekend rail trips we sometimes take with the children and hold eighty a month in cash. I'd apply now for the open council revenue-clerk vacancy if it is funded and the pay covers our mortgage, though it is still desk work. In the first year after 2028, if Foxbridge lets me go, I'd claim wage support immediately and ask the lender for temporary terms before a payment is missed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I can use AI every day and still lose my accounting job when the software gets cheaper than my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your partner say about the plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Mireya about the council application before sending it. She would probably offer extra sorting shifts, but those are seasonal and not guaranteed. We would tell the children about cancelled trips, not about a house sale we have not decided on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What exactly would you cut first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The first cut is rail fare, not the children's school meals. I'd put eighty in a separate account only if those trips are really cancelled. If the council vacancy closes, I would keep asking for funded posts while staying employed here.

say: I would demand a **wage bridge** for lost jobs.
I would seek **dates and notice** through the staff association.
think: My **screen job** may end soon after 2028, despite being an early user of the tools.
One **postal wage** cannot hold our mortgage.
do: Cancel **family rail trips** and hold eighty cash monthly.
Seek **mortgage-covering council work** only if funded; if the vacancy closes, ask for future funded posts while staying employed.
Claim **wage support** and request lender terms after dismissal.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about a lost wage and mortgage.
S2.quote: I can use AI every day and still lose my accounting job when the software gets cheaper than my wage.
fieldNote: **Thinking AI** reaches his junior accounting work in 2028, before robots matter.
The **rail fare cut** is real only if trips stop, while a council post depends on funding and pay.

steps.text: Cancel family rail trips and hold eighty monthly in cash
Apply for funded council revenue vacancy if wage covers mortgage
Seek wage support and lender terms after 2028 dismissal before missing mortgage payment
Seek next funded council openings if vacancy closes, while keeping current job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me get better at the work while finding a second path. I still expect AI to take most screen accounting in 2031, so I would not call a new tax certificate a safety net.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the firm to pay for moves into work clients still need, with paid hours to practice. I'd tell the association to press for vacancies to be offered to current staff before layoffs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn debt and benefits advice for families, though a thinking system might do parts of that too. The human conversation may last longer, but I need a real paying post and not just a course. Robots in 2034 do not extend my tax desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd enrol in the community debt-advice course this year only if Foxbridge covers the four-hundred fee and two paid study hours weekly. I'd ask the association to arrange a supervised case session at the local advice centre. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, if my tax post ends, I'd apply for a funded adviser vacancy only if its pay covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious but moving. Five years gives me time to test whether I can sit with someone whose bills are worse than mine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for study and time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Four hundred is more than we have spare after groceries. I'd ask for the fee and paid hours in writing, then use free advice-centre sessions if the firm refuses. I will not borrow for a job that might not exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would show the advice work fits you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want to help with one real case under supervision, not just watch an online lesson. If I cannot handle that conversation, I should find out while I still have this wage. A certificate alone will not pay the mortgage.

say: I would seek **paid study** tied to actual vacancies outside routine tax preparation.
I would ask for **internal offers** before layoffs.
think: Debt **advice work** may need a person but faces AI too.
A **funded wage** matters more than another certificate.
do: Study **debt advice** with employer-funded fee and two paid hours weekly; otherwise use free advice-centre sessions.
Take a **supervised case** if the advice centre permits.
Apply after 2031 for a **funded adviser role** if pay covers mortgage.
feel: I feel **anxious**, but able to test another path.
S3.quote: I will not borrow for a job that might not exist.
fieldNote: A **funded course** and paid hours are required because spare cash does not cover the fee.
A **supervised case** would test the emotional work before a later application.

steps.text: Take funded debt-advice course with two paid hours weekly; otherwise use free advice-centre sessions
Handle supervised advice case if centre permits access
Apply for funded adviser vacancy after 2031 if pay covers mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years might let my children finish school before accounting changes completely. I would be fifty-three by 2036, with less patience for chasing every software release but a lot more client experience.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the firm should share saved hours through shorter weeks and train workers while they still have wages. I'd ask local government to fund places for people whose jobs are disappearing, including older entrants like me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The return desk still faces thinking AI in 2036. I could move into community advice before then, if there are funded posts, but I cannot assume clients will pay directly. Robots in 2039 do not protect my current screen work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep using the tested letter tool and ask the advice centre next spring about a paid trainee place that covers the mortgage. I'd apply only if it has funding and supervised cases, and keep this accounting job while learning. In the first year after AGI in 2036, if Foxbridge closes my post, I'd take a funded advice vacancy if offered; otherwise I'd claim wage support and search again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though I can see enough years to make a careful turn. The mortgage still needs paying this winter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do your children enter the long plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My son would be nearly grown by 2036, but I will not ask him to finance the household. I want the years to give the children choices, not a bill for my career change. My children's future should not be our backup plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must the paid trainee place offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the advice centre for the paid trainee rate, a supervisor and a written route to a vacancy. If the rate does not cover our mortgage, I would keep my job and ask about later openings. I cannot use family savings that do not exist.

say: I would seek **shorter weeks** and paid transitions while workers still have wages.
I would support **public training places** for displaced workers.
think: A **funded advice post** could offer a route if wages cover home.
do: Keep **current accounting pay** and tested letters while learning, or if funded trainee terms fail.
Start **funded advice training** only with supervised real cases, a paid mortgage-covering rate and a written route to a vacancy.
After **2036 job loss**, take funded mortgage-covering advice work if offered; otherwise seek wage support while searching.
feel: I feel **anxious** because winter bills arrive first.
S4.quote: My children's future should not be our backup plan.
fieldNote: The **ten-year runway** lets him seek paid supervised advice work without assuming direct client income.
His **children** are not a financial fallback, and every move must cover the mortgage.

steps.text: Keep current accounting job and tested letters while learning or if trainee terms fail
Start funded advice traineeship with paid mortgage-covering wage, supervised cases and written vacancy route
Take funded mortgage-covering advice job if accounting post ends after 2036 and vacancy offered
Seek wage support while searching after 2036 post loss if no funded advice vacancy

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The system would reach my screen work before I had a second trade, and Mireya's wage cannot carry our mortgage. A wage bridge, lender flexibility and paid training linked to a funded vacancy would help. I like learning tools, but a new button does not make our mortgage smaller.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who gets the time saved by people like me. If faster letters let a junior learn tax codes on paid time, that is real progress. If the firm just gives me more files for the same low wage, I will still be behind at dinner.

headlineQuote: I like learning tools, but a new button does not make our mortgage smaller.
portrait: At **forty-three**, Victor is a junior tax accountant after adult study and earlier print-shop work.
His **accounting bachelor’s** and daily AI use have not yet lifted him above low pay or novice skill.
A **mortgage**, two schoolchildren and less than one month saved keep ordinary bills pressing.
Few **local firms** limit escape if junior hours shrink despite his early tool use.
He seeks **paid training** and tests supervised debt advice as a conditional route.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** threatens his screen job before another trade can support the mortgage.
whatWouldHelp: He wants a **wage bridge**, lender flexibility and paid training tied to funded work.
